records.label: What quantities, units, populations or specialist terms can you define before data arrive?
fields: What quantities, units, populations or specialist terms can you define before data arrive?
One useful note / Already done / Skip
No mandatory glossary or invented measurements.

records.label: Could you compare two feasible data methods or plan the first purposeful representation while you wait?
fields: Could you compare two feasible data methods or plan the first purposeful representation while you wait?
C20 method choices, C31 first-move plan
Planned methodology and diagrams aren't completed collection or observations.

records.label: This is SOURCE SEARCH, so keep candidates in private Pathfinder notes. Only when a verified source is ACTUALLY used should you write its selection rationale in the IA.
fields: This is SOURCE SEARCH, so keep candidates in private Pathfinder notes. Only when a verified source is ACTUALLY used should you write its selection rationale in the IA.
Record candidate / Check fit / Already checked
Aim, variables, relevant population, current data mode
A candidate URL isn't an IA data source until confirmed.

records.label: Do source definitions, units, population/time, accuracy, provenance and permissions support your intended maths and audience?
fields: Do source definitions, units, population/time, accuracy, provenance and permissions support your intended maths and audience?
Short contextual source-fit checks, not one giant form
Original data design, intended beneficiary and possible sources
Don't treat a source as used until accessible and verified; cite origin.

records.label: If this source answers a DIFFERENT question, would you like to revise the aim or keep looking?
fields: If this source answers a DIFFERENT question, would you like to revise the aim or keep looking?
Keep searching / Propose edit / Teacher check / Save
Original aim, predictions and proposed new source
No silent plan rewrite, retain original prediction and concerns.

records.label: What genuine observations do you have and what could their size, missingness, imbalance or accuracy prevent you concluding?
fields: What genuine observations do you have and what could their size, missingness, imbalance or accuracy prevent you concluding?
No fabricated values or unsupported population claims.

records.label: Is the problem the result, the next mathematics, software, writing, permission, deadline or something else?
fields: Is the problem the result, the next mathematics, software, writing, permission, deadline or something else?
One category / Other; jump to relevant existing helper
Current stage, actual method and flags
Don't open every checklist or conflate practical delays with IA mathematical limitations.

records.label: What's ONE useful thing you can do now, even if the original problem remains unresolved?
fields: What's ONE useful thing you can do now, even if the original problem remains unresolved?
Choose next stage/action / Own action / Not sure
Current issue, feasible alternatives, earlier drafts
No invented deadline or unnecessary full action plan.

records.label: Would you like to save this issue and return to your previous section later?
fields: Would you like to save this issue and return to your previous section later?
Return / Save; optional user-entered intended check date
Issue category, action, source notes and return stage
No automatic approval, issue resolution or implemented reminder.

records.label: Which is true: no usable data yet, some data but incomplete, accessible source found, or data verified and ready?
fields: Which is true: no usable data yet, some data but incomplete, accessible source found, or data verified and ready?
Confirm actual status / Skip if unchanged
Don't show actual maths as completed based on a planned source.

records.label: Just AFTER the ACTUAL result, write a concise local conclusion: what did this numerical/pictorial/theoretical result show about [aim]? If its accuracy or method changes the claim, acknowledge only the relevant new consequence.
fields: Just AFTER the ACTUAL result, write a concise local conclusion: what did this numerical/pictorial/theoretical result show about [aim]? If its accuracy or method changes the claim, acknowledge only the relevant new consequence.
Most recent actual resultRef, observed feature, aim/prediction/beneficiary, applicable C24 accuracy and prior limitation location.
Write immediately AFTER result; no routine-algebra prompts or a duplicated final conclusion.

records.label: From [previous actual result and local takeaway], what ONE worthwhile mathematical question remains?
fields: From [previous actual result and local takeaway], what ONE worthwhile mathematical question remains?
Own question / Enough for aim / Not sure
Previous resultRef, takeaway, aim and beneficiary
Available after first figure and every later substantive result; never force a new question.

records.label: Which actual mathematical question remains after the last aim-linked result, and WHY would [chosen technique] answer it? Check whether the earlier source/accuracy boundary affects that choice.
fields: Which actual mathematical question remains after the last aim-linked result, and WHY would [chosen technique] answer it? Check whether the earlier source/accuracy boundary affects that choice.
Choose method and WHY / Show 1–2 ideas / None
Current course, observation, previous methods and original aim
No disconnected extra mathematics or predetermined positive result.

records.label: Just AFTER [previous section takeaway] and BEFORE [next calculation], explain why [new method] follows and what it will investigate.
fields: Just AFTER [previous section takeaway] and BEFORE [next calculation], explain why [new method] follows and what it will investigate.
Write now / Already covered + ref / Show example / Defer
Previous resultRef, openQuestion, chosenMethod, writing-cue status
One or two sentences, in student's voice; no system-authored final prose.

records.label: Has the investigation now produced enough relevant, understood mathematics to answer the aim honestly, even if the answer is limited?
fields: Has the investigation now produced enough relevant, understood mathematics to answer the aim honestly, even if the answer is limited?
Continue / Conclude / Teacher check / Save / Not sure
Actual results, course level, aim and audience
No calculation quota; don't automatically grant a grade or final readiness.

records.label: You ACTUALLY calculated Pearson's r = [student's number] for [real paired variables]. What does it show about LINEAR association in this sample?
fields: You ACTUALLY calculated Pearson's r = [student's number] for [real paired variables]. What does it show about LINEAR association in this sample?
Actual r, variables, sample and observed scatter
Do not show for proposed r, predicted linearity or merely visual estimate.

records.label: If actual r and the scatter suggest a useful straight-line relationship, would fitting a line help predict [meaningful quantity] for [aim]?
fields: If actual r and the scatter suggest a useful straight-line relationship, would fitting a line help predict [meaningful quantity] for [aim]?
Optional line fit / Already enough / Other
Real r, scatter, course and whether aim needs estimation
Line is NOT compulsory and its validity/domain must be considered when actually fitted.

records.label: Your r shows little LINEAR association in this sample. Does the real scatter show curvature, groups, unusual points or restricted range worth investigating?
fields: Your r shows little LINEAR association in this sample. Does the real scatter show curvature, groups, unusual points or restricted range worth investigating?
One relevant check / Honest limited conclusion / None
Actual low/contextually weak r, confirmed plot feature and source
No claim there is NO relationship, no guessed curve, and no p-hacking.

records.label: If the linear prediction is unsupported and there's no convincing other pattern, is that finding itself meaningful for the original aim?
fields: If the linear prediction is unsupported and there's no convincing other pattern, is that finding itself meaningful for the original aim?
Conclude honestly / Justified alternative / Not sure
Actual r and scatter, original expectation, beneficiary
Never try correlations repeatedly until one becomes positive.

records.label: What exactly differs from [original prediction], and what real data feature or assumption would justify checking another interpretation?
fields: What exactly differs from [original prediction], and what real data feature or assumption would justify checking another interpretation?
Original prediction/WHY, actual r, graph and units
No point deletion, invented explanation or quiet change to earlier hypothesis.

records.label: Will your proposed regression/other measure answer a NEW worthwhile question, or just add more equations?
fields: Will your proposed regression/other measure answer a NEW worthwhile question, or just add more equations?
Useful / Not useful / Teacher check / Save
Most recent result and proposed next method
No automatic Spearman for every curve or rigid Pearson coefficient cut-offs.

records.label: What does the previous mathematical section conclude, and how does your next calculation follow from it?
fields: What does the previous mathematical section conclude, and how does your next calculation follow from it?
Short lead-in / Already covered / Not relevant
Latest real result and local takeaway
Use same logic for FIRST and ALL later substantive maths, not for each algebraic step.

records.label: RIGHT AFTER the new substantive result, what does it show about [aim]? When reporting its value, have you applied the earlier C24 measurement/source precision appropriately to this calculation? Does an ACTUAL new method limitation affect the claim?
fields: RIGHT AFTER the new substantive result, what does it show about [aim]? When reporting its value, have you applied the earlier C24 measurement/source precision appropriately to this calculation? Does an ACTUAL new method limitation affect the claim?
Observation, aim link, local takeaway, then C35
Actual output, novel accuracy issue, original aim/prediction
Ask aim connection first; accuracy and limitation cues only when materially relevant. Skip duplicate discussions and routine algebra; preserve original evidence and writing status.

records.label: Does another calculation genuinely help your investigation, or would your mathematical story be stronger by drawing things together now?
fields: Does another calculation genuinely help your investigation, or would your mathematical story be stronger by drawing things together now?
Continue for a reason / Conclude / Not sure
Result ledger, real course-level maths and conclusion status
Never require a fixed number of methods, figures or pleasing results.

records.label: Would a relevant example or teacher discussion help you choose the next method for THIS result?
fields: Would a relevant example or teacher discussion help you choose the next method for THIS result?
Keep help optional; no unsupported out-of-course technique.

records.label: If a result made you change model, data or method, how will you explain that change RIGHT HERE between sections?
fields: If a result made you change model, data or method, how will you explain that change RIGHT HERE between sections?
Write revised rationale / Already covered / N/A
Original plan, actual observation and new approach
Do not erase prior method/prediction or silently overwrite student text.

records.label: What is the ACTUAL source/resolution or justified uncertainty for [named quantity], in [units]? How might this affect later numerical results?
fields: What is the ACTUAL source/resolution or justified uncertainty for [named quantity], in [units]? How might this affect later numerical results?
Record / Edit / Not applicable; save working-vs-reporting policy
Real measurement/source, unit, resolution, any supported uncertainty and later intended use
Do not invent an error range from d.p. alone. Planning-only source has no confirmed numeric accuracy.

records.label: Earlier you recorded [C24 quantity + units + precision/source]. Does THIS graph's scale, labels and displayed accuracy respect it?
fields: Earlier you recorded [C24 quantity + units + precision/source]. Does THIS graph's scale, labels and displayed accuracy respect it?
Check figure / Already checked / Not relevant
Real plotted variables and their C24 input/source accuracy record
Primarily fix the graph, not write another limitations paragraph; no universal axis d.p. rule.

records.label: Just BEFORE this figure or calculation, what does it help you investigate about [aim]? Are any new units or variables clear to the reader?
fields: Just BEFORE this figure or calculation, what does it help you investigate about [aim]? Are any new units or variables clear to the reader?
Write short purpose / Already covered / Not relevant
Actual figure or calculation, aim/beneficiary, first-use definitions and relevant units
The earlier precision reminder may inform display; don't explain below-course plotting mechanics.

records.label: Directly AFTER [actual result], what does the value or observation MEAN for [current aim]? Could it change your prediction or advice to [beneficiary]?
fields: Directly AFTER [actual result], what does the value or observation MEAN for [current aim]? Could it change your prediction or advice to [beneficiary]?
Write 1–2 sentences / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Confirmed actual resultRef, current aim and beneficiary, original prediction
Prioritise aim over generic 'the graph shows'. No inference from imagined or planned results.

records.label: C24 recorded [source/resolution and units]. Does this ACTUAL derived result or diagram require different reporting precision or a NEW uncertainty qualification?
fields: C24 recorded [source/resolution and units]. Does this ACTUAL derived result or diagram require different reporting precision or a NEW uncertainty qualification?
Apply policy / Explain new effect / Already covered / Not relevant
Exact current operation/outputRef, input quantity records, prior written accuracy location
Keep sufficient working precision; don't simply carry raw decimal places into derived numbers or invent ±.

records.label: WHY does [the mathematical method you are about to use] answer the question raised by [previous real result] and help with [aim]?
fields: WHY does [the mathematical method you are about to use] answer the question raised by [previous real result] and help with [aim]?
Write one rationale / Already covered / Show example
Latest result/section takeaway, chosen ACTIVE technique, aim and any consequential precision limit
Never require a catalogue of alternatives or limitations of techniques not yet performed.

records.label: You used [recorded quantities and units] with [C24 resolution/source precision] in [calculation]. Are the reported units/digits for [ACTUAL output] defensible, and what does it show about [aim]?
fields: You used [recorded quantities and units] with [C24 resolution/source precision] in [calculation]. Are the reported units/digits for [ACTUAL output] defensible, and what does it show about [aim]?
Apply earlier rule / New effect / Already done / Not relevant
Real derived resultRef, operation, input refs, output units, earlier rule and any revisions
Do not assume input d.p. equals output d.p.; avoid premature rounding and fake bounds.

records.label: Only if the method has ACTUALLY been used: is there a specific assumption, domain or sensitivity which changes what [current result] can tell you about [aim]?
fields: Only if the method has ACTUALLY been used: is there a specific assumption, domain or sensitivity which changes what [current result] can tell you about [aim]?
Write with result / Already covered / Not relevant
Active technique, real output, source/sampling limitations already explained
Do not repeat practical difficulty or earlier caveat if it doesn't add a new mathematical consequence.

records.label: Considering what the previous result REALLY established and what its accuracy/scope can support, WHY would [chosen next technique] be the most logical next step for [aim]?
fields: Considering what the previous result REALLY established and what its accuracy/scope can support, WHY would [chosen next technique] be the most logical next step for [aim]?
Write brief bridge / Already covered / Show ideas / Enough—conclude
Last resultRef, aim-linked local takeaway, real relevant accuracy/scope, course
Do not demand extra maths or repeat a limitations paragraph at every transition.

records.label: For ACTUAL r or another statistic, what does the calculated value mean for [aim]? Report sensible precision for that statistic and consider only relevant data/method limits.
fields: For ACTUAL r or another statistic, what does the calculated value mean for [aim]? Report sensible precision for that statistic and consider only relevant data/method limits.
Interpret statistic / Already covered / Not relevant
Real statistic output, data quality/source context, sample and original aim
A dimensionless statistic doesn't automatically inherit raw input d.p.; no invented p-values or causation.

records.label: Did your later graphs, calculated results and predictions USE the earlier C24 decisions or explicitly justify a revision? Are aim interpretations and relevant limitations beside their results?
fields: Did your later graphs, calculated results and predictions USE the earlier C24 decisions or explicitly justify a revision? Are aim interpretations and relevant limitations beside their results?
Targeted return to affected work / Already consistent / Not relevant
C24 source policy, each accuracyUse/resultRef, aim-link and writing status
A presentation check, not a new evaluation chapter; preserve the student's earlier prose.

records.label: Is [technique] on my actual IB Maths course, partly an extension, outside, or am I unsure?
fields: Is [technique] on my actual IB Maths course, partly an extension, outside, or am I unsure?
Within / Partly / Beyond / Unsure / Ask teacher
Student's selected course/programme, active method and previous mathematical question
Verify topic status with student's actual syllabus or teacher; not automatically classified by tool. Independently researched and beyond-syllabus are separate flags.

records.label: This method is ON my course: can I use it correctly, showing my mathematics and WHY it helps [aim], without explaining how the method works?
fields: This method is ON my course: can I use it correctly, showing my mathematics and WHY it helps [aim], without explaining how the method works?
Proceed with working / Need technique help privately / Already covered
Verified in-course status; current technique, named quantities and aim
In the IA: normal calculations, purpose and contextual interpretation. NO textbook-style procedural explanation.

records.label: What is the central NEW mathematical idea in [technique]? Can I explain it briefly in MY words, demonstrate a relevant step/check and show why it is applicable?
fields: Confirmed beyond-course method at first use
What is the central NEW mathematical idea in [technique]? Can I explain it briefly in MY words, demonstrate a relevant step/check and show why it is applicable?
Own concept explanation / Check my understanding / Show example / Teacher check
Actual beyond-syllabus component, course, assumptions, own workings, research sources and aim
Explain only the necessary new maths beside FIRST use, not a full tutorial or copied formula. Cite the researched source.

records.label: Exactly which part of [technique] goes beyond my syllabus? Can I explain that extension without re-teaching the standard steps?
fields: Partly unfamiliar extension to taught maths
Exactly which part of [technique] goes beyond my syllabus? Can I explain that extension without re-teaching the standard steps?
Explain novel element / Already covered / Show example
Standard method, new extension, source, actual calculation, original question
At first use of NOVEL component; no exhaustive prerequisite derivation.

records.label: Before deciding how much I need to explain, can I check whether [technique] is covered by [selected maths course] and ask my teacher if necessary?
fields: Before deciding how much I need to explain, can I check whether [technique] is covered by [selected maths course] and ask my teacher if necessary?
Check syllabus / Teacher question / Keep Unsure and Save
Student-selected programme and actual technique ID, relevant source/version, unresolved teacher check
Private decision, not IA prose. Avoid inventing official syllabus verdicts or forcing irrelevant explanation.

records.label: What did I understand from [resource] that helps me carry out [technique] correctly? If new to the syllabus, what explanation do I need to include and cite?
fields: Student INDEPENDENTLY researched a mathematical idea now actually used
What did I understand from [resource] that helps me carry out [technique] correctly? If new to the syllabus, what explanation do I need to include and cite?
Own learning note / Link sources / Write explanation if beyond course
Genuine resource, actual method and its course classification, intended use
Research on an in-course idea does NOT require writing a tutorial. Include referenced mathematical sources appropriately.

records.label: Can I show that I truly understand the unfamiliar idea with a relevant relationship, short derivation, parameter explanation or checked example?
fields: Can I show that I truly understand the unfamiliar idea with a relevant relationship, short derivation, parameter explanation or checked example?
Brief demonstration / Already shown / Need help
Current mathematical formula/algorithm and its assumptions/actual application
At FIRST use. A copied equation or software screenshot alone does not demonstrate understanding.

records.label: Do I understand the mathematics that produced [actual output]? If the technique is new, what principle/condition must I explain?
fields: Actual software calculation relies on method unfamiliar or beyond course
Do I understand the mathematics that produced [actual output]? If the technique is new, what principle/condition must I explain?
Explain needed mathematics / Already covered / Verify / Course technique
Active algorithm, verified course status, actual tool output, aim and student source
If in course, interpret result without software tutorial; if outside, demonstrate relevant mathematical understanding in own writing.

records.label: Beyond what this result means for [aim], did I discover something NEW about a pattern, relationship, mathematical condition or method?
fields: Student genuinely learns something MATHEMATICAL from actual substantive result
Beyond what this result means for [aim], did I discover something NEW about a pattern, relationship, mathematical condition or method?
Short genuine insight / None / Already covered / Show example
Actual resultRef, student's previous understanding and aim-linked reflection
AFTER essential interpretation, beside the work. Optional; don't manufacture engagement or demand this after routine algebra.

records.label: Did this ACTUAL finding change how I understand two familiar mathematical ideas or when a technique can/cannot be used?
fields: Earlier taught maths yields a genuine new connection
Did this ACTUAL finding change how I understand two familiar mathematical ideas or when a technique can/cannot be used?
Write a precise new connection / None / Already covered
Actual working, observed mathematical contrast and previous interpretation
A genuine learning insight is allowed for syllabus maths; still NO how-to tutorial for the familiar technique.

records.label: Could a simpler, well-understood syllabus method answer [aim] better, or should I research the essential maths and check with my teacher?
fields: Student cannot explain a beyond-syllabus technique
Could a simpler, well-understood syllabus method answer [aim] better, or should I research the essential maths and check with my teacher?
Understand/research / Teacher check / Choose other maths / Save
Selected advanced technique, actual course, possible simpler alternatives, current investigation
No automatic rejection, but don't treat unexplained complexity as stronger mathematics.

records.label: Have I already explained this exact NEW mathematical idea where it first appeared, or does this section introduce genuinely different mathematics?
fields: Later new technique or source differs from first section
Have I already explained this exact NEW mathematical idea where it first appeared, or does this section introduce genuinely different mathematics?
Already covered + paragraph ref / New explanation / Not relevant
Saved first-use technique and explanationRef; actual later extension
Suppress repeated conceptual teaching; only explain a new component or substantive mathematical insight.

records.label: Did I spend pages explaining routine syllabus maths while leaving any independent, beyond-course technique unexplained? Can I correct the original passage and source citation?
fields: Did I spend pages explaining routine syllabus maths while leaving any independent, beyond-course technique unexplained? Can I correct the original passage and source citation?
Targeted edit at first use / Already clear / Teacher check
Actual selected course, syllabus/extension flags, own first-use explanations, source refs and result insights
This is a LOCAL revision checklist, not a new conclusion paragraph or automatic judgement of grade.

records.label: Who or what is your intended population, and what is one observation?
fields: Who or what is your intended population, and what is one observation?
Short description: target population, unit, scope
Target population ≠ the convenient people you can reach; distinguish sampling frame.
State which population the conclusions can reasonably apply to.

records.label: Could you include everyone (a census), rather than take a sample? What would that involve?
fields: When population is countable and potentially accessible
Could you include everyone (a census), rather than take a sample? What would that involve?
A census may make sense for a small school club; it need not be appropriate for all school students.
Judge the scope of the inference: census coverage, nonresponse and target-population mismatch matter mathematically; collection time by itself is a feasibility issue.

records.label: Which feasible methods could you use: simple random, stratified, systematic, cluster, opportunity/convenience or another?
fields: Which feasible methods could you use: simple random, stratified, systematic, cluster, opportunity/convenience or another?
Choose several to compare; optional Other
Show short definitions only when unfamiliar; don't overwhelm with method names.
Compare representativeness, coverage and potential bias for these methods; cost or convenience matters only if it changes what can reasonably be inferred.

records.label: How will people/observations actually be selected?
fields: How will people/observations actually be selected?
If claiming random selection, describe an implementable random procedure; avoid saying 'random' when volunteers opt in.
Explain how the chosen procedure affects selection bias and reproducibility.

records.label: Why is your sample size or accessible population adequate for what you want to compare?
fields: If using a sample or census
Why is your sample size or accessible population adequate for what you want to compare?
More data can help, but size alone doesn't eliminate bias. Consider balanced groups and what is achievable.
Discuss effect of sample size on stability of estimates and comparisons, and distinguish small samples from selection bias. Do not make blanket claims about adequate size.

records.label: Who might not respond, and what kind of bias could this introduce?
fields: Who might not respond, and what kind of bias could this introduce?
Volunteer responses and nonresponse may systematically differ from those who did not answer.
Explain how you'll reduce bias, or limit the conclusions to the respondents.

records.label: Are questions neutral, clear and measurable? Have you tested them with a small pilot?
fields: Are questions neutral, clear and measurable? Have you tested them with a small pilot?
Short pilot check; examples when requested
Define what rating scales represent; don't treat '5/5 happiness' as a physical measurement to arbitrary precision.
Prioritise response bias, the validity of scales and what may be inferred from scores; piloting matters when it improves measurement validity, not as a logistical story.

records.label: Are the measurements paired correctly, using the same observation and compatible units?
fields: Two numerical quantities measured per subject
Are the measurements paired correctly, using the same observation and compatible units?
Record height and reaction time for each person as a pair, not unmatched lists.
Assess measurement repeatability and whether potential confounding variables matter.

records.label: How were groups defined, and are measurement conditions reasonably comparable?
fields: How were groups defined, and are measurement conditions reasonably comparable?
Different times, tools or ages may affect results as well as the factor being compared.
Justify fair comparison and explain important confounders/unequal group sizes.

records.label: How was the original dataset sampled or measured, who produced it, and which population does it represent?
fields: How was the original dataset sampled or measured, who produced it, and which population does it represent?
You can choose a dataset, not retroactively choose its original sampling design.
Evaluate fit for the aim and cite sampling/method limitations honestly.

records.label: What will you include/exclude, and how could that choice change your conclusions?
fields: If data have missing values, filtering or outliers
What will you include/exclude, and how could that choice change your conclusions?
Don't discard inconvenient observations just to create the predicted correlation.
Justify filtering, record missing data and test sensitivity where feasible.

records.label: Could the timing/location of collection distort the apparent pattern?
fields: If data change with location, date or season
Could the timing/location of collection distort the apparent pattern?
A lunchtime survey might not describe morning behaviour; one season may not represent the year.
Justify scope and when it is reasonable to generalise.

records.label: Is your model based on collected measurements, existing published values, theoretical assumptions or a combination?
fields: Is your model based on collected measurements, existing published values, theoretical assumptions or a combination?
Not every model needs a statistical sample. A theoretical optimisation may need dimensions and constraints instead.
Only ask collection/sampling questions that apply to actual sources.

records.label: Which inputs, parameters, constraints and units does your model need, and where will they come from?
fields: When model has inputs or parameters
Which inputs, parameters, constraints and units does your model need, and where will they come from?
For a storage-box model: L, w, h and volume V; note dimensions and constraints.
Justify how each important value relates to the real situation and intended use.

records.label: What feasible ways could you measure or estimate these inputs? Why prefer your chosen tool/source?
fields: What feasible ways could you measure or estimate these inputs? Why prefer your chosen tool/source?

Compare phone-video timing and a handheld stopwatch in terms of time resolution, reaction-time variation, repeatability and possible systematic bias; equipment inconvenience alone is not a mathematical limitation.
Explain how the method affects estimated parameters, numerical accuracy and model fit. Mention practical effort only briefly when it changes the quality or amount of evidence.

records.label: Can readings be repeated, conditions controlled or instruments checked?
fields: When repeated empirical readings are feasible
Can readings be repeated, conditions controlled or instruments checked?
Repeat measurements can reveal variation, but repeated readings do not fix a systematic error.
Explain the likely dominant error and what can be controlled.

records.label: Which assumptions make the model manageable, and are they acceptable for its intended purpose?
fields: Which assumptions make the model manageable, and are they acceptable for its intended purpose?
Ignoring air resistance might work for a short low-speed example, but not all trajectories.
Explain which assumptions affect the mathematical validity of the model and over what range. A convenient simplification is acceptable only if the consequence for results is limited and justified.

records.label: Are the units, definitions, coverage and original measurement context of each source suitable?
fields: Using estimated or published model parameters
Are the units, definitions, coverage and original measurement context of each source suitable?
Published constants/measurements may apply only within particular environments or scales.
Attribute sources; explain context differences and uncertainty where known.

records.label: How will you check the model on real observations, ideally not exactly those used to fit its parameters?
fields: For models that can be tested against observations
How will you check the model on real observations, ideally not exactly those used to fit its parameters?
A separate test or held-out observations is helpful when there are enough data, but isn't mandatory in every IA.
Distinguish a model fitting its original data from an independent check; a lack of validation limits confidence in model predictions, not just project logistics.

records.label: What other model could plausibly describe the situation, and how might you choose?
fields: If deciding between different model forms
What other model could plausibly describe the situation, and how might you choose?
Linear vs exponential growth; compare context and residual behaviour rather than expected trend alone.
Justify a sensible fit and interpretable parameters.

records.label: What range of input values/conditions is your model intended for?
fields: If model is useful only over a limited domain
What range of input values/conditions is your model intended for?
An empirical model may not justify extrapolation far beyond measured inputs.
Outside the observed/input range, conclusions may be extrapolations that the mathematics cannot justify; restrict the domain or explicitly qualify the result.

records.label: If a key measurement/parameter changes slightly, how much does the result change?
fields: When parameters are estimated or measurements uncertain
If a key measurement/parameter changes slightly, how much does the result change?
Small changes in measured radius may affect calculated volume noticeably.
Use reasonable sensitivity/uncertainty rather than fabricated precision.

records.label: Are the input observations sampled? Would a census or a different sampling method improve the model's relevance?
fields: If a modelling investigation also uses survey/sample observations
Are the input observations sampled? Would a census or a different sampling method improve the model's relevance?
Fitting a model to sampled data requires understanding sample bias and scope.
Avoid treating modelling and statistics as mutually exclusive.

records.label: What simple theoretical case or constraint demonstrates that the model is worth investigating?
fields: If model has little/no collected data
What simple theoretical case or constraint demonstrates that the model is worth investigating?
For constrained optimisation, a diagram with correctly named lengths can be more useful than arbitrary collected data.
Explain assumptions without inventing a dataset or a sampling plan.

records.label: What mathematical object, claim, condition or simplified case are you investigating?
fields: What mathematical object, claim, condition or simplified case are you investigating?
No requirement for a population or sampling procedure.
Give a meaningful definition and explain why the approach is suitable.

records.label: Which assumptions, specialist terms, restrictions and notational choices must the reader understand?
fields: If applying ideas to a special context
Which assumptions, specialist terms, restrictions and notational choices must the reader understand?
Define the mathematical object precisely; introduce deeper techniques at first use.
State which conclusions follow from the assumptions or special cases. The fact that a proof/problem was time-consuming is not a mathematical limitation.

records.label: What aspect would you like to confirm with your teacher before relying on this method?
fields: Unusual method or different course route
What aspect would you like to confirm with your teacher before relying on this method?
Keep the teacher-check-in branch and summary available.
Do not mark the mathematical approach as approved automatically.

records.label: What TWO or more plausible approaches could have produced useful evidence?
fields: What TWO or more plausible approaches could have produced useful evidence?
Only compare realistic choices the student could genuinely carry out; include sample/census or available datasets.
Evaluate methods primarily by their mathematical consequences: quality of measurements, representativeness, bias, assumptions and validity of conclusions.

records.label: Which approach did you actually choose, and WHY is it preferable for your investigation?
fields: Which approach did you actually choose, and WHY is it preferable for your investigation?
'It was easier' is not a sufficient mathematical justification. Explain why the chosen method produces evidence suitable for the aim, with acceptable error and inferential scope.
Practical feasibility may explain the selection of a method, but the discussion of limitations must focus on how the choice affects numerical results or conclusions.

Biased probabilities or unjustified independence assumptions change conditional probabilities and expected outcomes.
Compare estimated probabilities across groups/conditions and identify assumption sources.
State the decision context and restrict expected-value advice to supported probabilities.
Require an actual probability-based method, not a vague prediction.
Student is calculating conditional probability/expected value using estimates and assumptions that can be checked.

records.label: AI23 / AA20 / AA25; measured time
fields: Could reaction-time variation affect calculated speed, acceleration or rates?
Timing variation can have a larger effect on derived quantities for short intervals; excessive reported decimals are misleading.
Take repeated timings where feasible, compare variability or a better-supported timing method.
Sufficient for an approximate trend only when uncertainty does not change the conclusion.
Do not equate stopwatch display resolution with true accuracy.
Timing measurements actually collected by manual stopwatch; discuss measurement variability/resolution at source.

records.label: AI23 / AA20 / AA25
fields: Could frame rate, frame selection or camera positioning limit timing accuracy?
Quantisation of video time steps and perspective can affect parameter estimates.
Identify frame interval and physical scaling; check sensitivity to one-frame shifts.
Defensible at a time scale much larger than frame uncertainty, with appropriate precision.
Only suggest if video-based measurements were selected.
Timing/distance from video frames actually collected; discuss frame and calibration limits at source.

records.label: AI11 / AA11 / AA22
fields: Could a small uncertainty in a length affect an area or volume estimate noticeably?
Squaring/cubing dimensions can amplify percentage uncertainty in derived areas or volumes.
Recalculate using plausible upper/lower measurement values or a simple sensitivity check.
Report a precision/range that reflects input measurements and relevant geometry.
Never assume a specific instrument tolerance without verifying it.
Student is now using measured lengths in area/volume or other nonlinear geometry calculations; consider how input uncertainty changes the RESULT.

records.label: AI06 / AA03 / AA07; M02
fields: Is a constant percentage change realistic over your entire chosen period?
Exponential models can diverge from real data when growth saturates, conditions change or rate is not constant.
Inspect residuals/observations over time and compare with a sensible alternative model.
Use only over a justified time interval; avoid long-term claims unsupported by data.
No assertion of an upper bound unless context supports one.
Student is actively constructing/using an exponential model; check its assumptions and useful period.

records.label: AI05 / AA06; M03
fields: Could the polynomial fit measured points but behave unrealistically between or beyond them?
High-order curves can fit noise, produce artificial turning points and give unstable extrapolation.
Compare a simpler model, inspect residuals and graph outside the sample range only to test plausibility.
Restrict to a sensible domain; avoid treating a fitted turning point as physically meaningful automatically.
A true quadratic derived from geometry need not have data overfit; check fitted-vs-theoretical context.
Student is actively fitting/interpreting a polynomial data model; distinguish from a theoretically derived polynomial.

records.label: AI08 / AA08; M04
fields: Have you observed enough cycles to estimate the period and amplitude convincingly?
A short sequence may fit an apparent cycle that is actually a trend or irregular fluctuation.
Inspect several cycles where possible; compare phase/period stability and model residuals.
Interpret repeating behaviour only over supported conditions and duration.
Don't claim every oscillating graph is periodic.
Student is actively fitting/interpreting a periodic or sinusoidal model; cycles and period estimation can be evaluated.

records.label: AI24 / AA22; M03/M06
fields: Does your optimum obey the real constraints, including endpoints and allowed dimensions?
A stationary point might be infeasible or give a local, not global, optimum; discrete design choices also matter.
Identify domain/constraints; check boundaries, feasibility and alternatives around the optimum.
Recommend an optimum only for the stated model and realistic constraints.
Don't equate differentiating to zero with proof of a global optimum.
Student is finding/checking an optimum with differentiation or a model; include constraints/endpoints and interpretation.

records.label: AI07 / AA03 / AA07; M05
fields: Could the model depend strongly on the range of observed positive values?
A power model fitted over a narrow range may extrapolate poorly; log transformations exclude zero/nonpositive values.
Check domain, units, plot fit/residuals and sensitivity to high/low observations.
Report model only for justified positive inputs and observed-scale conditions.
Only show for a power relationship/transform actually being used.
Student is using a power law or transformed fit; positive-domain and fitted-range constraints are relevant.

records.label: AI12
fields: Does straight-line distance represent the 'closest' option people would actually use?
Euclidean proximity may disagree with road travel time, barriers or accessibility.
Compare a few locations using a realistic travel measure where available.
Interpret Voronoi cells as nearest in the CHOSEN metric, not automatically best service.
AI SL-specific current menu; do not assume real-world accessibility is Euclidean.
Student is constructing/interpreting a Voronoi model for locations; check the distance metric and practical meaning.

records.label: AI23 / AA20 / AA25
fields: Rates of change inferred from empirical data
Could small variations in measured values become much larger when estimating their rate of change?
Finite differences or derivatives estimated from noisy data can be unstable.
Try reasonable intervals or smooth-model comparisons, noting how each changes the estimate.
Use rate claims only at time/space resolution supported by evidence.
If differentiation is purely analytic, measurement noise may not apply.
Student is calculating/inferencing rates of change from empirically measured noisy data, not doing purely symbolic differentiation.

records.label: AI26; numeric samples
fields: Trapezoidal rule or numerical integration chosen
Could the spacing between data points miss important curvature?
Numerical area estimates may depend on step size when the function changes rapidly.
Compare estimates with finer spacing where available or a sensible alternative approximation.
State that the numerical estimate applies at the available sampling resolution.
AI SL catalogue option; don't assert definite error bounds without justified conditions.
Student is actively applying trapezoidal rule/numerical integration to sampled values; review spacing and curvature.

records.label: AI09 / AI15 / AA16; M07
fields: Did you assess the model only with the same observations used to fit it?
Good in-sample fit does not automatically demonstrate predictive accuracy on new cases.
Where feasible, compare against separate observations or describe the lack of independent validation.
Use careful within-sample conclusions if independent testing is unavailable.
Not every theoretical model requires empirical validation; only if claiming predictive fit.
Student is fitting/testing a predictive model and interpreting model fit or accuracy; compare calibration/validation evidence.

records.label: AI10 / AI11 / AA12 / AA25; M06
fields: Which simplifying assumption most changes the result when relaxed?
Neglecting friction/air resistance or treating an object as uniform can alter predicted motion/optimisation.
Compare two plausible parameter values or a more realistic case; discuss magnitude and applicability.
Retain simplification only if it doesn't change the intended practical decision materially.
Do not introduce assumptions (e.g. friction) irrelevant to the chosen model.
Student is using a model with an identifiable simplifying assumption whose effect can be checked.

records.label: AA04; T01
fields: Mathematical claim inferred only from several numerical examples
Have you established a general claim, or only checked some examples?
A pattern observed for several inputs may fail for an untested case; examples alone do not prove all cases.
Seek a valid proof or identify conditions/possible counterexamples.
Phrase a conjecture as a conjecture until justified; restrict claims to tested cases if necessary.
Do not frame every theoretical exploration as requiring proof of a universal statement.
Student is now arguing a general mathematical claim from numerical examples; proof/scope is at issue.

records.label: AA04 / AA09; T01
fields: Algebraic derivation uses restricted domains or special cases
Could the result fail at an excluded value or outside the stated domain?
Division by an expression, inverse operations or square roots may require excluded cases or introduce extraneous solutions.
Check zero denominators, domain restrictions and converse implications; test boundary cases.
State precisely the set of inputs/conditions for which the result holds.
Use only when such algebraic restrictions actually arise.
Student is doing algebra/proof involving inverses, division, roots or domain restrictions; exclusions matter now.

records.label: AI15 / AA16; M02/M04
fields: Time-series observations or repeated measures from same subjects
Could observations that are close together in time or from one person be dependent?
Independence assumptions for tests or error analysis may not hold; apparent sample size can overstate information.
Inspect grouping/time ordering; compare per-person trends or residual patterns when relevant.
Conclude about the observed series/conditions and avoid unjustified independent-sample tests.
Don't impose an advanced independence test; focus on appropriate interpretation.
Student is now using repeated/time-series observations in a test, regression or model where dependence assumptions matter.

records.label: AI13 / AA14; data resolution
fields: Could the recorded precision, upper limit or detection threshold hide meaningful variation?
Rounded or censored input values limit distinguishable differences and numerical precision of derived results.
Check source definitions/precision and examine whether plausible variation changes calculations or rankings.
Report results only to defensible precision and avoid conclusions about changes smaller than measurement resolution.
Only applicable where source values truly have coarse rounding or thresholds.
Collected/source values are rounded, capped, censored or resolution-limited, which needs documenting before later mathematics.
